title: Action Figures
summary: The Huntik Action Figures are a range of fully articulated figures based on Season 1 of Huntik: Secrets & Seekers. They were manufactured by Big Bocca and released by Upper Deck in December 2009, being sold in the UK, US and across Europe. The range consisted of three lines, the Seeker Figures, the Titan Figures and the Titan Deluxe Figures.

sections.heading: Development and Unreleased Figures
sections.wikitext:
Upper Deck's Huntik toy line was developed based on the early episodes of [[Season 1]] of the television series. The range consisted of three waves, the 6" Seeker Figures, the 6" Titan Figures and the larger Titan Deluxe Figures which were 8"-9" in size. The line began rolling out at the end of 2009, being sold in the UK, US and in Italy and Europe. 

Several figures that were planned and designed for the line were ultimately cancelled and never mass produced. The most notable of these was the [[Sophie Casterwill]] action figure which never made it past the prototype stage, making her the only original main character not to have a figure released. A fully completed [[Suit]] prototype modelled on [[Mr. Koskin]] was also produced, but, again, never went into mass production. Nevertheless, both figures were still advertised on the back of the Seeker figures packaging. 

For the Titan figures, a fully completed figure of [[Freelancer]] was produced, but never went into mass production. It was nevertheless advertised on the back of the Titan figures packaging. It would have included lance and shield accessories and a cut-out Amulet. An [[Ammit Heart-Eater]] figure was also fully sculpted and painted but never mass produced. This figure was never advertised or listed on product packaging, suggesting that several more figures were planned for additional waves of the line that were based on some of the later episodes of the first season. 

Upper Deck would later discontinue its Huntik merchandise the following year, and while no official explanation was ever given for this, it can be attributed to the toy line's release coinciding with the company's growing financial difficulties and eventual bankruptancy. 

In 2011, a new line of [[Lights & Sounds Action Figures]] was released by [[Giochi Preziosi]], the new toy master, for [[Season 2]]. These figures were of the same scale as the Upper Deck figures and thus served as a spiritual successor to the original 2009 line.

full_text:
The Huntik Action Figures are a range of fully articulated figures based on Season 1 of Huntik: Secrets & Seekers. They were manufactured by Big Bocca and released by Upper Deck in December 2009, being sold in the UK, US and across Europe. The range consisted of three lines, the Seeker Figures, the Titan Figures and the Titan Deluxe Figures. 

== Development and Unreleased Figures ==
Upper Deck's Huntik toy line was developed based on the early episodes of Season 1 of the television series. The range consisted of three waves, the 6" Seeker Figures, the 6" Titan Figures and the larger Titan Deluxe Figures which were 8"-9" in size. The line began rolling out at the end of 2009, being sold in the UK, US and in Italy and Europe. 

Several figures that were planned and designed for the line were ultimately cancelled and never mass produced. The most notable of these was the Sophie Casterwill action figure which never made it past the prototype stage, making her the only original main character not to have a figure released. A fully completed Suit prototype modelled on Mr. Koskin was also produced, but, again, never went into mass production. Nevertheless, both figures were still advertised on the back of the Seeker figures packaging. 

For the Titan figures, a fully completed figure of Freelancer was produced, but never went into mass production. It was nevertheless advertised on the back of the Titan figures packaging. It would have included lance and shield accessories and a cut-out Amulet. An Ammit Heart-Eater figure was also fully sculpted and painted but never mass produced. This figure was never advertised or listed on product packaging, suggesting that several more figures were planned for additional waves of the line that were based on some of the later episodes of the first season. 

Upper Deck would later discontinue its Huntik merchandise the following year, and while no official explanation was ever given for this, it can be attributed to the toy line's release coinciding with the company's growing financial difficulties and eventual bankruptancy. 

In 2011, a new line of Lights & Sounds Action Figures was released by Giochi Preziosi, the new toy master, for Season 2. These figures were of the same scale as the Upper Deck figures and thus served as a spiritual successor to the original 2009 line.
